newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Royalist election candidate killed in Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Royalist election candidate killed in Cambodia.

text.p: Gunmen have killed a royalist candidate for local polls in northwest Cambodia, triggering fears his death could mark the start of pre-election violence.

Vorn Chhunly, a member of the royalist FUNCINCPEC party and police chief in Battambang province, said by telephone on Tuesday that unidentified gunmen shot dead Soeurng Sophin and his two sons on Thursday.
The dead man was a commune chief in the northwest rice-bowl province and a FUNCINPEC candidate for local elections, which are due to be held later this year or in 1998.
The polls are expected to be fiercely contested by the rival FUNCINPEC and Cambodian People's Party (CPP), which formed an uneasy coalition after U.N.-run elections in 1993.

The two, who fell out last year over FUNCINPEC's demand for a greater share of power, have effectively been campaigning for some months but no deaths have been directly related to the local and general polls due this year and next.
"We don't have enough evidence (to accuse anyone)," said Vorn Chhunly.

One analyst said such incidents could be expected in politicised provinces such as Battambang, especially ahead of local elections, where long-time CPP incumbents will face challenges for the first time in years.
Supporters of the two main parties in the coalition government clashed for several days earlier this month in the province, leaving casualties on both sides.

The fighting only ended when the co-Defence Ministers Tea Banh (CPP) and Tea Chamrath (FUNCINPEC) were sent to Battambang on Friday to cool tempers and following the recall of the two most senior provincial and military officials from each side.
FUNCINPEC Secretary General Loy Sim Chheang said he could not comment on the matter as a joint commission had been set up to investigate such incidents.
